To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the HAC absorption feature in z~2 is more detectable and the water ice feature less detectable than in local ULIRGs.
The detection of PAH features in the rest-frame 2um region is consistent with a starburst-dominated nature for the sources.
the HAC absorption features are more common and the water ice absorption features less common than expected from local samples, but consistent with an expected higher AGN fraction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evolution of dust properties in galaxies, in particular the evolution of dust composition and the evolution of dust temperatures.
the evolution of the dust in the early universe.
the evolution of the dust properties and PAH features in ULIRGs from z~0 to z~2.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our sample of z~2 sources is similar to local ULIRGs in that the 3-8um spectrum is dominated by the hot dust continuum, but that the ice-to-dust ratio is lower, and that the HAC absorption is detectable in more sources than expected from local samples.
the PAH and HAC features are detected in starburst-dominated ULIRS, but the water ice feature is detected only in a few cases.
the ice and HAC detections are in agreement with the idea of an AGN-dominated sample.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have confirmed a more AGN dominated sample of ULIRGs, with the exception of one source.
these ULIRGs have a similar mix of AGN and starburst activity as local ULIRGs.

, on average, the z~2 ULIRS show similar dust properties to the local ULIRGs but with a higher AGN component, and a slightly lower ice-to-silice ratio, which may be due to the shorter timescale for ice formation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we are able to confirm the presence of a large reservoir of molecular material in the inner regions of these z~2 ULIGRs, and that these molecular species are present even in AGN dominated systems.
the ice and HACs in these z~2 ULIRS are not necessarily more evolved than local ULIRGs.

, despite being heavily absorbed in the rest-frame mid-IR, the dust in these z~2 ULIRS is not as cold as in the local universe, and that there may be a trend for the ice-to-dust ratio to decrease at high-z.
